usage: This is the standard way to ask how someone is in Modern Standard Arabic. It is used in formal writing, news broadcasts, and literature, though rarely in casual conversation where local dialects dominate. The pronoun suffix changes depending on the gender and number of the people being addressed.

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: Used when addressing a single female.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Used when addressing three or more people, or a mixed-gender group.

variants.label: to two people
variants.note: Used specifically when addressing exactly two people.

variants.label: gender-neutral / general
variants.note: A general way to ask how things are without specifying gender.

examples.arabic: مَرْحَباً يَا أَحْمَد، كَيْفَ حَالُكَ الْيَوْمَ؟
examples.english: Hello Ahmad, how are you today?
Madam, how are you after the trip?
